answer_text:
Let

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}
\frac{1}{mnp(m+n+p+1)}.
\]

Use the integral representation

\[
\frac{1}{m+n+p+1}=\int_0^1 x^{m+n+p}\,dx.
\]

Since all terms are nonnegative, we may interchange summation and integration:

\[
S=\int_0^1 \sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}
\frac{x^{m+n+p}}{mnp}\,dx.
\]

The triple sum factors:

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}
\frac{x^{m+n+p}}{mnp}
=
\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^m}{m}\right)
\left(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n}\right)
\left(\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^p}{p}\right).
\]

For \(0\le x<1\),

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^k}{k}=-\ln(1-x).
\]

Thus

\[
S=\int_0^1 \bigl[-\ln(1-x)\bigr]^3\,dx.
\]

Now substitute

\[
u=-\ln(1-x),
\qquad x=1-e^{-u},
\qquad dx=e^{-u}\,du.
\]

As \(x\) goes from \(0\) to \(1\), \(u\) goes from \(0\) to \(\infty\). Therefore

\[
S=\int_0^\infty u^3 e^{-u}\,du.
\]

This is the Gamma function evaluated at \(4\):

\[
\int_0^\infty u^3 e^{-u}\,du=\Gamma(4)=3!=6.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{6}
\]
